material_definitions: Solid electrolytes based on lithium titanium phosphate were prepared.
The materials studied are substitution systems Li(1+x)Ti2Si(z)P(3-x)O12 and Li(1+x)M(x)Ti(2-x)(PO4)3 where M3+ = Al3+, Cr3+, Ga3+, Fe3+, Sc3+, In3+, Lu3+, Y3+, and La3+.
These materials are derived from LiTi2(PO4)3 by partially replacing Ti4+ with M3+ and P5+ with Si4+ ions.

The samples were prepared as sintered pellets, and the conductivity enhancement is attributed to the increase of the sintered pellet density and enhancement of the lithium concentration at the grain boundaries.
The solid electrolyte based on the Li(1+x)Ti2SixP(3-x)O12 system were synthesized.
Sintering was conducted at 1473 K for 2h.
The porosity of the sintered pellets decreased remarkably and the conductivities were greatly enhanced with the increase of Si4+ substitution.
The solid electrolytes based on the LiTi2(PO4)3 prepared in this study were synthesized via substitution of M3+ ions for Ti4+ sites, resulting in the Li(1+x)M(x)Ti(2-x)(PO4)3 systems.
These materials generally possess a rhombohedral (R-3C) structure.
The sintering property is closely related to the ionic radius of the M3+ ion.
The conductivity for the sample of Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 showed the maximum value for all the M3+ substitution systems.
